text:
maria: noticed a p95/p99 uptick right after today's runtime v2.14 canary rollout. p95 +40ms, p99 +220ms for text-gen route in us-west-2 :frowning:
kevin: ack. which cohort? customer-facing or internal traffic?
maria: looks like customer cohort C3 (high-concurrency, short-seq). spikes concentrated on hotpath nodes tagged runtime=v2.14-kernelB.
nora: logs show a lot of auth plugin retries around the same time (502->retry->200). maybe token fetch latency added to tail.
sam: interesting — we also changed kernel selector heuristics in this build (prefer kernelB for >512 tokens). but the cohort is short-seq (<200). suggests selector misfire or metric leak.
leo: deploy-bot: canary finished at 10:12, 12% traffic. rollback not triggered.
deploy-bot: Deployment v2.14 -> canary 2026-03-16T10:12Z. healthchecks: PASS.
kevin: can we reproduce with a synthetic cohort that mirrors C3? run the workload generator against canary nodes.
maria: started a short run: command: 
```
./loadgen --target https://canary-usw2.api.redwood.ai/generate \
  --concurrency 200 --qps 800 --seq-len 120 --model redwood-open-7b
```
kevin: also add header Authorization to emulate token fetch path (auth service) and enable KV cache cold start path.
maria: dump of 1% traces attached: many traces show a blocking call to auth.client.get_token ~150ms occasionally, then runtime spends ~60ms compiling kernelB path.
nora: stack snippets: `auth_proxy: fetch_token -> cache_miss -> async refresh`, `kernel_selector: lock contention -> selection fallback -> JIT warm path`
sam: hypothesis: combined effect of auth refresh jitter + kernelB JIT/warmup causing tail. either kernel selector is choosing kernelB for short seq due to stale telemetry, or runtime misreports seq distribution.
kevin: what's the p99 breakdown by step? frontend latency vs server runtime vs auth vs net?
maria: quick sample: p99_total=680ms, p99_runtime_infer=340ms, p99_auth=160ms, p99_net+proxy=80ms. runtime-infer spikes correlated with node label kernelB.
leo: any config flips in yesterday's PRs? I remember a scheduler-affinity tweak and a selector threshold tweak. PRs: #4221 (selector threshold), #4239 (scheduler affinity).
kevin: can we bisect selector behavior? i.e., force kernelA on canary and compare.
nora: yeah, we can set env REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=kernelA on a subset of canary hosts (5%) and run loadgen.
maria: doing that now on canary hosts canary-3a/3b.
ora: also increasing auth token cache TTL on canary to avoid refresh storms: REDWOOD_AUTH_TTL_OVERRIDE=300s.
kevin: good. if p99 drops with kernelA forced + auth TTL bump then we narrow root cause to selector + auth interplay.
maria: quick results: when forcing kernelA p99_runtime_infer drops from 340ms -> 160ms. overall p99_total down to ~430ms. auth TTL bump further drops to ~370ms.
sam: that points to kernel selector misrouting to kernelB causing warmup/JIT penalty even on short sequences, amplified by auth refresh adding extra tail time.
leo: mitigation path? options:
- revert selector change in next rollback.
- pin affected tenants to runtime v2.13 until we fix.
- increase auth token TTL temporarily cluster-wide.
- add soft fallback: if seq_len < 256 choose kernelA.
kevin: short-term: roll back selector change (PR #4221) from canary and promote. mid-term: add runtime guard to prevent kernelB for short sequences. long-term: improve selector telemetry and add async JIT warmup for hot nodes.
maria: opening rollback runbook now. cc @support-escalations for customer comms.
leo: deploy-bot: rolling config change (remove PR #4221) to canary subset.
ora: also patch auth config to TTL 300s cluster-wide via feature flag `auth.ttl.override=300`.
deploy-bot: applied config change to canary-1..canary-4 at 10:28Z. healthchecks still PASS.
maria: monitoring: after rollback of selector, p99_runtime_infer back to ~165ms in canary. p99_total ~410ms. still slightly above baseline but auth TTL patch pending.
kevin: plan: 1) Promote rollback to 50% traffic after 10m observation. 2) Patch auth TTL globally. 3) Run bisection test with selector change isolated to confirm root cause.
sam: for reproducibility notes: to simulate auth jitter, set `AUTH_PROXY_DELAY_MS=120` in loadgen. to simulate cold kvcache, restart runtime before load.
ora: repro script: 
```
# warmup off, clear cache
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-canary-3a
sleep 5
./loadgen --target https://canary-usw2.api... --concurrency 200 --seq-len 120 \
  --auth-header 'Bearer $TEST_TOKEN' --auth-proxy-delay 120
```
maria: customer comms draft: "We observed an increase in tail latency for short-sequence workloads after a canary rollout. We've rolled back the kernel selector change and applied a temporary auth TTL patch. We're monitoring and will follow up with a permanent fix."
kevin: any billing/auth impacts? billing looks fine. some customers reported degraded UX, support tickets created.
leo: created incident ticket INC-2026-0812 and linked support threads.
sam: followups: add guard in selector code, add telemetry for per-node kernel choices, and implement background JIT warm on kernel switch.
maria: assigning follow-ups: kevin -> selector guard + bisect; nora -> auth TTL feature flag + metrics; sam -> JIT-warm work item.
kevin: grabbing this now. will post PR link.
maria: thanks everyone. I'll update #customer-success and post timeline when baseline fully restored. :thumbsup:
leo: closing note: if anyone sees p99 re-emerge, ping @pager and add a short trace in #slo-alerts.
sam: +1
deploy-bot: canary rollback complete at 10:34Z.
